title: Note React Parity
description: Get the note technology (note/plugin/rs + framework/renderer/react) to premigration feature level (git tag `premigration`, where note/react/index.tsx was a 1069-line React renderer — NoteCanvas with 6 block kinds, 10 tools, marquee/resize/ink/erasers, contentEditable rich-text + table-cell editors, clipboard paste, KaTeX math, navigator minimap, undo/redo, keybindings, SVG/PNG export — plus note/core/js's NotePlayController) for the react renderer on the migrated Rust plugin architecture: note/plugin/rs emits UiTree interpreted by framework/renderer/react. Follow the approach of PUZZLE-2D-REACT-PARITY and PUZZLE-3D-REACT-PARITY (26/07/09). Core design: add a dedicated note-canvas componentKind + NoteCanvasHost (DOM-based, mirrors puzzle2d-board precedent) since the generic canvas-2d host cannot render rich text/tables/KaTeX math. Gesture protocol via applyNoteEvents{eventsJson,phase,selectIds} with begin/live/commit/atomic undo boundaries.
summary: Restored note to premigration feature level on the migrated Rust-plugin architecture. Added a dedicated `note-canvas` SurfaceKind/NoteCanvasScene wire type (mirroring the puzzle2d-board precedent) since the generic canvas-2d host can't render rich text/tables/KaTeX math. Built a new DOM-based `NoteCanvasHost` React component porting the premigration `NoteCanvas` (grid, pan/zoom, direct+marquee selection, 8-handle resize, pencil ink, both erasers, contentEditable rich-text + table-cell editors, clipboard paste of blocks/images/SVG/text, navigator minimap, KaTeX math with fallback). Implemented an `applyNoteEvents` gesture protocol (begin/live/commit/atomic phases) so drag/resize/ink/erase gestures each produce exactly one undo step regardless of pointermove count, verified by dedicated Rust tests. Filled Rust model/command gaps: rich text marks, image assets map, grid subdivisions/opacity, table row/column ops, fixed duplicate (now offsets +24/+24 and re-ids group children recursively), setActiveExample/setFixtureJson/saveDownload/loadRequest, and full shell chrome (window measures/engagements/toolbar/keybindings). Verified via 18 Rust unit tests, 8 dedicated React unit tests (64/64 total suite), and a wasm-verify.ts script driving the actual compiled plugin end-to-end (example load, gesture undo-boundary, engagements, measures, tools, manifest) — all passed. Live browser verification was attempted but blocked by an unrelated multi-writer race on the shared framework/plugin/registry/generated/plugins.ts file from other concurrent dev sessions in the same checkout (documented in verify-log.md); a browser-verify.ts script is left ready to run once only one scoped dev server is active.
